session.title: PCP jump-line quality touch - capped
session.purpose: Keep jump timing, pump, landing quietness, and DH-line confidence sharp after a high-load Kiara day without adding meaningful recovery debt before Sabbath rest.

dose.run_count: 2 warm-up/assessment runs plus up to 2 quality runs
dose.cap: Four DH/jump-line runs maximum; no new features, no lap-time chasing, no extra volume.
dose.focus: Pump timing, squash/absorb timing, quiet landings, braking discipline into corners, and relaxed upper body.
dose.driving_context: Driver coaching is mild cognitive stress in an air-conditioned car; keep fueling/hydration steady so it does not become recovery drag.

session.adaptation_hypothesis: A capped PCP session can preserve technical timing and confidence while the nervous system is still recovering from Friday's enduro load; extra runs would likely add impact and sympathetic cost faster than they add skill.
execution_rules: Use the first run as a body check, not a speed check.
Keep every run at 80-90% aggression with clean timing.
Rest fully between runs; do not start the next run while breathing, grip, or focus is still elevated.
Repeat the same line and same cues; do not introduce a new feature or setup variable.
Eat and hydrate before driver coaching; do not arrive depleted.

expected_result.garmin_load: low-to-moderate, with technical impact cost higher than the HR load may show
expected_result.rpe: easy to moderate, never survival or race-like
expected_result.next_day: Sabbath rest with no upper-body hangover, heavy legs, or elevated stress response
expected_result.technical_result: Each run should feel equally timed or cleaner; no progressive decline in pop, braking, or landing quietness.

stop_rules: Stop after two runs if timing feels late, landings get heavy, or upper-body tension appears.
Stop immediately after any casing, near-miss, sketchy save, or repeated braking mistake.
No fourth run unless run three is technically cleaner than run two.
Do not extend the session because the body feels good; yesterday's load is the limiter.
